images.title: Place values are powers of 10
images.purpose: Shows 5642 in a place value chart whose column headings are 10³, 10², 10¹ and 10⁰.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. One four-column place value chart in the centre with a heading row and one digit row.
images.exact_structure: A table with exactly 4 equal columns and 2 rows, thin dark outline. Heading row, filled light teal (#0072B2), left to right: '10³', '10²', '10¹', '10⁰'. Digit row, large digits left to right: '5', '6', '4', '2', each in amber (#E69F00). No other marks.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Each place value is a power of 10.
images.description: Shows 5642 in a place value chart whose column headings are 10³, 10², 10¹ and 10⁰.
images.context: 5000 + 600 + 40 + 2 = 5642. After the decimal point the places continue as 10 to the powers −1, −2, −3.
images.teaching_notes: Ask what heading would come to the right of 10⁰ for a decimal.

image_decisions.why: Seeing each place value column headed by a power of 10 is the core of expanded form with powers of 10.
